'''Jrue Randall Holiday''' ({{IPAc-en|d|r|uː}} {{respell|DROO}};<ref>{{Cite press release |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |date=October 24, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |access-date=May 17, 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517083503/https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |author=<!--Not stated-->}}</ref> born June 12, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for one season with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] before being selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the first round of the [[2009 NBA draft]] with the 17th overall pick.

Holiday played four seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers before being traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in 2013. In 2020, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and won his first [[NBA championship]] with the team in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]. Holiday was later traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] via the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2023 and won his second NBA championship with the team in [[2024 NBA Finals|2024]] before being traded back to Portland in the 2025 offseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=June 4, 2025 |title=Sources: Celtics trading Holiday to Trail Blazers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45572537/celtics-trading-jrue-holiday-trail-blazers-sources-say |access-date=December 13, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=December 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251224203854/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45572537/celtics-trading-jrue-holiday-trail-blazers-sources-say |url-status=live }}</ref> Holiday is a two-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and six-time [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] member. He also won a gold medal with the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020]] and [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 U.S. Olympic team]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HOLIDAY Jrue |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/jrue-holiday_1954709 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240823153259/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/jrue-holiday_1954709 |archive-date=August 23, 2024 |website=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]]}}</ref>

==Early life==
Holiday was born to Shawn & Toya (''née'' DeCree)  Holiday.<ref name="hayes_0625201">{{Cite news |last=Hayes |first=Marcus |date=June 25, 2018 |title=The true Jrue Holiday |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/sixers/20130215_Marcus_Hayes_.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130218011316/http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/sixers/20130215_Marcus_Hayes_.html |archive-date=February 18, 2013 |work=Philadelphia Daily News}}</ref> His parents both played college basketball at [[Arizona State Sun Devils|Arizona State]],<ref name=hayes_0625201/> where Toya was named [[Pac-12 Conference Women's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]] in 1982.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Elling |first=Steve |date=December 3, 1987 |title=Trading Places : Ex-Kennedy Star Toya Holiday Returns as Coach of City's Premier Girls Program |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-12-03-sp-26373-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208193716/http://articles.latimes.com/1987-12-03/sports/sp-26373_1_kennedy-high |archive-date=December 8, 2015 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> Holiday attended [[Campbell Hall School]] in the Los Angeles district of [[Studio City, California]]. As a senior, he averaged 25.9 points, 11.2 rebounds, 6.9 assists, 4.8 steals per game. The team went 31–5 and won the California Division IV state title. Holiday was rated the No. 1 point guard and the No. 2 overall prospect in the Class of 2008 by [[Rivals.com]]. He was named the 2008 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] and a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' first-team All-American]]. Holiday also played in the [[2008 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], tallying 14 points, five rebounds, three assists, and five steals.<ref name="nbabio">{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday stats, details, videos, news |url=http://www.nba.com/players/jrue/holiday/201950 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171216140417/http://www.nba.com/players/jrue/holiday/201950 |archive-date=December 16, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Off the court, he was a member of Campbell Hall's gospel choir, the percussion section leader in the school's orchestra, and the manager of the school's girls' tennis team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday named Gatorade P.O.Y. |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/jrue_holiday_named_gatorade_poy_080326.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927233130/https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/jrue_holiday_named_gatorade_poy_080326.html |archive-date=September 27, 2023 |access-date=September 27, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Weiss |first=Jared |date=May 21, 2024 |title=How Jrue Holiday found his voice as a leader with help from his soccer star wife |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5499499/2024/05/21/jrue-holiday-boston-celtics-lauren-us-soccer/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521104121/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5499499/2024/05/21/jrue-holiday-boston-celtics-lauren-us-soccer/ |archive-date=May 21, 2024 |access-date=May 21, 2024 |work=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>

==College career==
In [[2008–09 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2008–09]], Holiday played alongside fellow future NBA player [[Darren Collison]] in the backcourt at [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maikis |first=Jason |date=June 24, 2019 |title=Commemorating the anniversaries of some of UCLA's most memorable NBA drafts |url=http://dailybruin.com/2019/06/24/commemorating-the-anniversaries-of-some-of-uclas-most-memorable-nba-drafts/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210045211/http://dailybruin.com/2019/06/24/commemorating-the-anniversaries-of-some-of-uclas-most-memorable-nba-drafts/ |archive-date=December 10, 2019 |access-date=December 10, 2019 |website=Daily Bruin}}</ref> In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 8.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.6 steals in 27.1 minutes per game. Holiday shot 45.0% from the floor, 30.7% from three-point range and 72.6% from the line, earning Pac-10 All-Freshman Team honors. He scored a career-high 20 points on a perfect 8-of-8 shooting in just 19 minutes of play against [[FIU Panthers men's basketball|Florida International]]. Holiday had 13 points and six assists in UCLA's one-point win over [[2008–09 VCU Rams men's basketball team|Virginia Commonwealth]] in the first round of the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].<ref name="nbabio" /> After the season, he [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|declared for the NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2009 |title=UCLA's Holiday will declare for NBA Draft |url=http://www.sbsun.com/2009/04/09/uclas-holiday-will-declare-for-nba-draft/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211105032/http://www.sbsun.com/2009/04/09/uclas-holiday-will-declare-for-nba-draft/ |archive-date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=sbsun.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Jrue Holiday To Remain In NBA Draft |url=http://pac-12.com/article/2009/06/13/jrue-holiday-remain-nba-draft |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211105055/http://pac-12.com/article/2009/06/13/jrue-holiday-remain-nba-draft |archive-date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=pac-12.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia 76ers (2009–2013)===
====Early years (2009–2012)====
Holiday was drafted 17th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2009.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629053745/http://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2009.html |archive-date=June 29, 2009 |access-date=December 10, 2019 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> On April 3, 2010, he scored a season-high 25 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday 2009-10 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2010/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211105035/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2010/ |archive-date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=basketball-reference.com}}</ref>

On November 5, 2010, Holiday set a new career high with 29 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. On February 2, 2011, he recorded his first career triple-double with 11 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists against the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday 2010-11 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212031439/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2011/ |archive-date=December 12, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=basketball-reference.com}}</ref>

On March 17, 2012, Holiday set a new career high with 30 points against the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday 2011-12 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2012/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212031443/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2012/ |archive-date=December 12, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=basketball-reference.com}}</ref>

====First All-Star selection (2012–2013)====
[[File:Jrue Holiday 76ers.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Holiday going against [[Kevin Séraphin]] of the Wizards in March 2013]]
Prior to the start of the season, Holiday signed a four-year, $41 million extension through the 2016–2017 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2012 |title=Jrue Holiday gets 4-year extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8578806/jrue-holiday-philadelphia-76ers-agree-contract-extension |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On November 25, 2012, Holiday set a new career high with 33 points against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On January 2, 2013, he recorded his second career triple-double with 16 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists against the Suns. On January 18, Holiday matched his career high with 33 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Eight days later, he scored a career-high 35 points against the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday 2012-13 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2013/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212031513/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holidjr01/gamelog/2013/ |archive-date=December 12, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=basketball-reference.com}}</ref> On January 24, Holiday was selected as a reserve for the Eastern Conference All-Star team for the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game]]. With his first All-Star selection, the 22-year-old Holiday became the youngest player in franchise history to be named an All-Star.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 24, 2013 |title=Jrue Holiday Selected To First All-Star Game |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/jrue-holiday-selected-first-all-star-game/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211105437/http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/jrue-holiday-selected-first-all-star-game/ |archive-date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2013–2020)===
====Injuries and comeback (2013–2017)====
[[File:20140101 Jrue Holiday (cropped).JPG|thumb|upright|Holiday in January 2014]]
On July 12, 2013, Holiday was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Nerlens Noel]] and the Pelicans' [[2014 NBA draft|2014]] first-round draft pick.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 12, 2013 |title=PELICANS ACQUIRE ALL STAR POINT GUARD JRUE HOLIDAY AND 2ND ROUND PICK PIERRE JACKSON IN EXCHANGE FOR TWO FIRST ROUND PICKS |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-all-star-point-guard-jrue-holiday-and-second-round-pick-pierre-jackson |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130715231339/http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-all-star-point-guard-jrue-holiday-and-second-round-pick-pierre-jackson |archive-date=July 15, 2013 |access-date=July 12, 2013 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> His [[2013–14 New Orleans Pelicans season|2013–14 season]] ended prematurely after season-ending surgery in February 2014 for a [[stress fracture]] in his right [[tibia]]. Holiday had not played since January 8 due to the shin injury. In 34 games, he averaged 14.3 points, 7.9 assists and 1.6 steals per game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2014 |title=Jrue Holiday out for season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10535006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211160824/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10535006/jrue-holiday-new-orleans-pelicans-surgery-season |archive-date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=December 10, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On January 5, 2015, against the [[Washington Wizards]], Holiday reached 5,000 career points.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2015 |title=Pelicans' Holiday reaches 5,000 point milestone |url=https://www.foxsports.com/southwest/story/pelicans-holiday-reaches-5-000-point-milestone-010515 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150113194042/http://www.foxsports.com/southwest/story/pelicans-holiday-reaches-5-000-point-milestone-010515 |archive-date=January 13, 2015 |access-date=January 5, 2015 |website=FoxSports.com}}</ref> On February 18, he was ruled out for three weeks after aggravating an already injured lower right leg.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 18, 2015 |title=Jrue Holiday Injury Update |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jrue-holiday-injury-update-1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220214032/http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jrue-holiday-injury-update-1 |archive-date=February 20, 2015 |access-date=February 18, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Holiday returned to action much later than originally expected, coming off the bench against the [[Phoenix Suns]] on April 10 after missing 41 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 10, 2015 |title=Davis scores 19 to help Pelicans beat Suns 90-75 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150410/PHXNOP/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211175549/http://www.nba.com/games/20150410/PHXNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=April 10, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On March 9, 2016, Holiday scored a career-high 38 points against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 9, 2016 |title=Hornets, Walker top Pelicans 122-113 for 5th straight win |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160309/NOPCHA/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626222927/https://www.nba.com/games/20160309/NOPCHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 26, 2019 |access-date=March 10, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 29, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after being diagnosed with a right interior orbital wall fracture.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 29, 2016 |title=Pelicans Announce Medical Updates |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-announce-medical-updates |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331053237/http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-announce-medical-updates |archive-date=March 31, 2016 |access-date=March 30, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On November 18, 2016, Holiday made his season debut after missing the Pelicans' first 12 games while on a leave of absence to care for his wife. In 23 minutes off the bench, Holiday scored 21 points on 8-of-14 shooting in a 113–101 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name="espn">{{Cite web |date=November 18, 2016 |title=Jrue Holiday makes splash, nets 21 in season debut for Pelicans |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899627 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120003317/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899627 |archive-date=November 20, 2016 |access-date=November 19, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On January 23, 2017, he had 33 points and 10 assists in a 124–122 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 23, 2017 |title=Jones, Holiday lead Pelicans past Cavs 124-122 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900092 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170125161348/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900092 |archive-date=January 25, 2017 |access-date=January 24, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==== 2020–21 season: Sportsmanship Award and First NBA championship ====

On November 24, 2020, Holiday was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a four-team trade, involving the [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], in which the Pelicans acquired [[Eric Bledsoe]], [[Steven Adams]], and draft compensation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2020 |title=Milwaukee Bucks Acquire Jrue Holiday From The New Orleans Pelicans As Part Of Four-Team Deal |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-acquire-jrue-holiday-new-orleans-pelicans-part-four-team-deal |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210104112314/https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-acquire-jrue-holiday-new-orleans-pelicans-part-four-team-deal |archive-date=January 4, 2021 |access-date=November 24, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==National team career==
Holiday was a member of the USA select team that trained with and against the 2012 national team. In 2013, he participated in the national team minicamp. 

He was selected to the national team for the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020/21 Olympics]] where USA finished with a 5-1 record and won gold. He started five of six games, averaging 11.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists. He won his second gold with the national team at the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 Olympics]] where he averaged 7.6 points, 1.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday |url=https://www.usab.com/players/jrue-holiday |access-date=April 26, 2026 |website=USA Basketball |language=en}}</ref>

While Holiday was approaching his seat, a young girl asked if he was [[Darren Collison]] and asked for his autograph. After explaining that he was not Collison and preparing to take his seat, Cheney, who was seated behind him, said, "Don't worry, you're cuter than Darren." At the time, both were in relationships with others, but they became friends, and began dating after Holiday was drafted by the 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maine |first=D'Arcy |date=June 25, 2015 |title=How Jrue Holiday Became the USWNT's Biggest Fan |url=https://www.espn.com/espnw/news-commentary/2015worldcup/story/_/id/13148436 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151115112401/http://espn.go.com/espnw/news-commentary/2015worldcup/article/13148436/how-jrue-holiday-became-uswnt-biggest-fan |archive-date=November 15, 2015 |access-date=October 13, 2015 |website=[[ESPNW.com]]}}</ref> They later began hosting annual combo basketball and soccer clinics at UCLA.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uWXZEx6hVIc |title=Two Sport Couple: Jrue and Lauren Holiday |date=September 11, 2015 |access-date=September 14, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925130217/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uWXZEx6hVIc&gl=US&hl=en |archive-date=September 25, 2015 |url-status=live |via=YouTube}}</ref>

In September 2016, Holiday took indefinite leave from the Pelicans to care for Lauren after she was diagnosed with a brain tumor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Jeff |date=September 4, 2016 |title=Jrue Holiday to miss start of season as pregnant wife Lauren Holiday faces brain surgery |url=http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2016/09/jrue_holiday_asks_for_prayers.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904162115/http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2016/09/jrue_holiday_asks_for_prayers.html |archive-date=September 4, 2016 |access-date=September 4, 2016 |website=NOLA.com}}</ref> The following month, Lauren had brain surgery only weeks after giving birth to the couple's daughter, J.T. (Jrue Tyler).<ref name="espn" /> They had their second child, a boy named Hendrix, in late 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ellis |first=Preston |date=December 2, 2020 |title=New Orleans was home: Jrue and Lauren Holiday discuss hardship of leaving but are excited to team with Giannis and Bucks |url=https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2020/12/2/21867891/jrue-holiday-giannis-nba-new-orleans-pelicans-lauren-milwaukee-bucks-mike-guevara-nba-smoothie-king |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211114181415/https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2020/12/2/21867891/jrue-holiday-giannis-nba-new-orleans-pelicans-lauren-milwaukee-bucks-mike-guevara-nba-smoothie-king |archive-date=November 14, 2021 |access-date=February 25, 2021 |website=thebirdwrites}}</ref>

Holiday is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He has said, "I'm a Christian athlete who has faith in [[Jesus Christ]]. So when I encounter circumstances over which I have no control, I believe and have peace."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jrue Holiday: NBA All-Star on Training, Nutrition & Family |url=https://www.livemomentous.com/blogs/momentous/jrue-holiday |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191226061116/https://www.livemomentous.com/blogs/momentous/jrue-holiday |archive-date=December 26, 2019 |access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref>
